provenance.note: `Challenges` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would. The clock and the agent's key are pinned. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode and the word list are the pinned tests' own and have never protected anything.

declarations.challenge_type: Challenge: { words: string[]; dt?: string; said?: string; authenticated?: boolean; };

deferred_capability.deferred_to: Roadmap 7.7 — Exchange endpoint retrieval and submission
deferred_capability.body: { const hab = await this.client.identifiers().get(name); const exchanges = this.client.exchanges(); const resp = await exchanges.send( name, 'challenge', hab, '/challenge/response', { words: words }, {}, [recipient] ); return resp; }
deferred_capability.send_body: { for (const recipient of recipients) { const [exn, sigs, atc] = await this.createExchangeMessage( sender, route, payload, embeds, recipient ); return await this.sendFromEvents( name, topic, exn, sigs, atc, recipients ); } throw new Error('recipients list was empty'); }
deferred_capability.create_body: { const keeper = this.client.manager!.get(sender); const [exn, end] = exchange( route, payload, sender['prefix'], recipient, datetime, dig, undefined, embeds ); const sigs = await keeper.sign(b(exn.raw)); return [exn, sigs, d(end)]; }
deferred_capability.send_from_events_body: data: any = { tpc: topic, exn: exn.sad, sigs: sigs, atc: atc, rec: recipients, }
deferred_capability.note: `respond` reads the habitat and calls `exchanges.send(...)`; `send` calls `createExchangeMessage`, which signs with the identifier's keeper, and then `sendFromEvents`, which POSTs `{tpc, exn, sigs, atc, rec}` to `/identifiers/{name}/exchanges`. All three are `Exchanges` methods, which `PORTING.md` §5.10 assigns to Roadmap 7.7 and which Roadmap 7.4 does not list as a prerequisite.
deferred_capability.rust_decision: moved to Roadmap 7.7 in §5.13 rather than duplicated here. Reproducing `sendFromEvents` would mean implementing the next roadmap item alongside this one: the generic exchange submission is 7.7's whole write half, not scaffolding for this single caller.

pinned_confirmations.note: the pinned `Challenges` case covers all four methods; the three in scope here are driven directly. It asserts the generated path, both verification paths, the word list in `verify`'s body, and the SAID in `responded`'s. The integration suites add the second strength, the operation `verify` returns, and the fact that a contact's challenge list starts empty — which is what `responded` is for.

the_strength_is_interpolated_not_validat.note: `strength: number` is stringified straight into the query, so a fraction reaches the wire as `1.5`, `NaN` as `NaN`, and a negative as `-1` — none of which any BIP39 generator accepts, and all of which the agent is asked for
the_strength_is_interpolated_not_validat.rust_decision: **refused**: `ChallengeStrength` accepts only the five entropy sizes BIP39 defines, so a request that could not produce a mnemonic cannot be written. keripy's own generator is the corroboration — it hands the value to `mnemonic.Mnemonic.generate(strength=…)`, which raises outside that set — recorded as corroboration rather than as a governing reference (ADR `0009`).

the_strength_default_is_observable.note: `generate(strength = 128)` writes the default into the query, so an omitted strength is still a request that names one
the_strength_default_is_observable.rust_decision: the strength is a required argument and `ChallengeStrength::BITS_128` names the reference's value, so what reaches the query is visible at the call site — Roadmap 7.1's `DEFAULT_ROLE` decision applied again

the_source_is_not_encoded.note: both verification paths are `/challenges_verify/${source}`, so a value carrying `/` or `?` addresses a different resource — and Roadmap 3.10 signs `@path`
the_source_is_not_encoded.rust_decision: refused twice over: the argument is Roadmap 3.4's validated `IdentifierPrefix`, and Roadmap 5.3's builder would encode it exactly once regardless

the_two_verification_calls_share_one_add.note: `verify` and `responded` address the identical path and differ only in method and body — `POST` asks the agent to check, `PUT` records that a caller accepted the answer
the_two_verification_calls_share_one_add.rust_decision: reproduced, with the segment pinned as one constant so the two cannot drift apart

responded_returns_the_raw_response.note: `responded` is the only method in the family that does not call `res.json()`: it returns the platform `Response` object itself, so a caller receives an unread body and a transport type
responded_returns_the_raw_response.rust_decision: returns `()`, which is what Roadmap 6.5's `delete` and Roadmap 7.3's do for the same reason — a non-success status is already `ClientError::Status`, and leaking a transport type across the SDK boundary is what `ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.7 exists to prevent

an_empty_word_list_is_accepted.note: `verify(source, [])` sends `{"words":[]}`, asking the agent to confirm that an identifier signed nothing
an_empty_word_list_is_accepted.rust_decision: **refused**, which is what Roadmap 6.12 did for an empty recipient list on the same reasoning: it is a caller mistake rather than a request, and a verification that trivially matches is worse than one that fails

the_answers_are_cast_rather_than_decoded.note: `generate` and `verify` return `res.json()` cast to `Challenge` and `ChallengeOperation`, so an answer of any shape reaches the caller — including one carrying no words at all
the_answers_are_cast_rather_than_decoded.rust_decision: decoded: both recorded wrong-shaped answers are proven refused, which is the rule Roadmap 6.8, 6.10, 7.1, and 7.3 applied to their own answers

the_said_reaches_the_body_not_the_path.note: `responded`'s `said` is written into the JSON body rather than the path, so unlike the source it cannot change an address whatever it holds
the_said_reaches_the_body_not_the_path.rust_decision: still typed as Roadmap 3.3's validated `Said`, because what it names is a specific exchange message and an unparseable one records an acceptance of nothing — the narrowing costs nothing the reference can usefully send
